disposition_reason: The main report says lead was found in every honey composite and gives honey's mean lead as 0.024 mg/kg (nd=LOR), 4th highest of 88 foods. Per-food tables (Appendix 3, Table A 3.4) are not in this PDF, so honey Cd, tAs and tHg values are not available here.
disposition_locator: Lead, Analytical results, printed p.47 (PDF p.48), text-copy lines 2115-2120; Table 7, printed p.48 (PDF p.49), text-copy line 2150

study.material_scope: Honey as one of 88 ATDS foods, prepared to a ready-to-eat state (honey needs no preparation), analysed as composites
study.growing_origin_vs_market: Bought at retail in Australian states and territories (Australian purchase market). National foods came from 4 jurisdictions and regional foods from all 8. Honey's class and production origin are not reported in the main report.
study.collection_period: 13-24 May 2013 (autumn) and 17-28 February 2014 (summer), ATDS-wide (printed p.17, text-copy line 770-771)
study.sampling_unit: composite samples, each made from 3 individual retail purchases from one state or territory. 508 composites across 88 foods. Honey's composite count is not stated: 4 for a national food, 8 for a regional food; the classification is in Appendix 1, which is not in file.
study.method: ICP-MS after acid digestion for cadmium, lead, mercury and total arsenic, at Symbio Laboratories, Brisbane, using NATA-accredited methods (Table 2, printed p.19)
study.lod_loq: Cd, Pb, Hg, As: LOR 0.005 mg/kg (water 0.0001 mg/L). The LOR equals the LOD, and the LOQ is 5 x LOD = 0.025 mg/kg (Table 2 and footnote, printed p.19).
study.basis: ready-to-eat (as consumed). For honey this is the same as as-purchased fresh weight.
study.qa: NATA-accredited methods for metals. No CRM or recovery data in the main report.

findings.material: honey (ATDS food; floral type not reported)
findings.group: Honey (all ATDS honey composites, May 2013 + Feb 2014)

reported.text: Several foods were determined to have lead in all of their respective composite samples including ... honey ... The highest mean concentrations (assuming nd=LOR) were detected in ... honey (0.024 mg/kg). | Table 7: Honey 25th ATDS 0.024 (mean lead concentration mg/kg, nd=LOR)

findings.censoring: Mean stated as nd=LOR (upper bound). The report says lead was detected in ALL honey composites, so no substitution applies: lower and upper bound are equal at 24 ug/kg. The mean (24 ug/kg) is below the stated LOQ (5 x LOD = 25 ug/kg), so some or all composites may have been detected but below the LOQ.
findings.locator: Lead, Analytical results, printed p.47 (PDF p.48), text-copy lines 2115-2120; Table 7, printed p.48 (PDF p.49), text-copy line 2150
findings.notes: Ranked 4th highest mean lead of 88 foods (after mussels 0.074, sultanas 0.037, chocolate cake 0.026). Table 7 comparators for honey, all secondary citations and not entered as findings: 23rd ATDS 0.052; US FDA 0.004 (lower bound, FDA TDS 2006-2013); EFSA 0.041 (EFSA 2012b); NZ 0.010 (middle bound, NZ MAF 2011). Exposure context: honey contributed 6% of estimated lead exposure for children aged 2-5 years and was a minor contributor for other age groups (printed p.49-50, text-copy line 2236-2237). The executive summary lists honey among the major dietary contributors to lead (text-copy line 283-286).

controls.control: Comparison of composite results with Food Standards Code Schedule 19 maximum levels for lead
controls.outcome: No composite sample in the study exceeded its corresponding ML. The report does not say whether an ML applies to honey.
controls.locator: Comparison against MLs and international levels, printed p.47 (PDF p.48), text-copy line 2122-2126

contradictions_with_stored_summary: No numeric contradiction: the wiki's honey mean of 0.024 mg/kg (nd=LOR) matches.

Wiki front matter has sampling_year_range: null and sampling_locations: [], but the body and primary text give May 2013 and February 2014 across Australian states and territories. This is an internal wiki inconsistency.
The wiki says foods were bought 'in all states and territories'. The primary text says national foods were bought in only four jurisdictions (printed p.17). Honey's class is unknown.

The wiki leaves out three honey-specific facts in the primary text: Pb was detected in all honey composites; the Table 7 honey comparators (23rd ATDS 0.052, US FDA 0.004, EFSA 0.041, NZ 0.010 mg/kg); and honey's 6% share of lead exposure for children aged 2-5.
unresolved: Appendix 3 (Table A 3.4 lead; A 3.2 arsenic; A 3.3 cadmium; mercury table) is not in this PDF. Honey's composite count, min/max/median Pb and its Cd, tAs and tHg results cannot be extracted from this file, though all foods were analysed for metal contaminants (printed p.17).
Honey's national vs regional classification (Appendix 1) is not in file, so n composites (4 or 8) is unconfirmed.

Three other library copies of this report also run to 69 pages with no appendices. A file named FSANZ_25th_ATDS.pdf in 'Manual Fetch Kimi /June 8/.../Australia/' returned no pdfinfo page count and no text (possibly corrupt); it was not used.
In the primary text, the honey mean (24 ug/kg) is just below the stated LOQ (25 ug/kg). Whether individual honey composites were quantified or only detected is not stated.
